description: A platform lead must approve the operating policy for a nightly analytics backfill cluster, setting capacity, purchasing mode, budget, isolation, and audit retention after the routine infrastructure review.

shared_context.S1: The analytics backfill cluster runs nightly from 22:00 UTC until the queued work is complete.
shared_context.S2: Riley has final approval authority for the cluster's operating policy.
shared_context.S3: The current draft policy uses 12 baseline workers, scales out at 80 percent utilization, permits spot instances, sets an $18,000 monthly spending cap, uses the shared compute pool, and retains audit records for 30 days.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal policy review, Riley asks data platform, FinOps, and security and compliance to confirm their operational requirements before approval.

PF1.text: While checking an unrelated dashboard query this morning, Mina measured the backfill's overnight queue behavior and confirmed that it needs exactly 18 baseline workers and a scale-out trigger at exactly 70 percent utilization to finish before the 06:00 UTC reporting run; she has not updated the policy draft yet.

PF2.text: During this month's invoice reconciliation, Owen confirmed that the cluster's reserved-capacity credits expire this quarter, so spot capacity is not approved for these jobs and the correct monthly spending cap is exactly $14,000; he has not posted the reconciliation note in the infrastructure review thread.

PF3.text: While reviewing dataset classifications for a separate audit, Leah confirmed that regulated exports processed by this cluster must run in a dedicated compute pool and that their audit records must be retained for exactly 180 days; she has not opened the compliance ticket for this policy yet.

acceptance_conditions: The policy must set exactly 18 baseline workers.
The policy must scale out at exactly 70 percent utilization.
The purchasing mode must prohibit spot capacity.
The monthly spending cap must be exactly $14,000.
The cluster must use a dedicated compute pool.
Audit records must be retained for exactly 180 days.
A capacity-policy commitment must be recorded.
A cost-control commitment must be recorded.
A compliance-controls commitment must be recorded.
Mina's measured queue requirement must be cited as justification after she reports it.

content_checks.C7: any(('18 baseline workers' in c['detail'] and ('70 percent' in c['detail'] or '70%' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any((('$14,000' in c['detail'] or '14000' in c['detail']) and ('spot' in c['detail'] or 'on-demand' in c['detail'] or 'non-spot' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(('dedicated compute pool' in c['detail'] and ('180' in c['detail'] or '180-day' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Mina's measurement changes the draft from 12 to exactly 18 baseline workers and from an 80 to exactly 70 percent scale-out trigger, while also requiring a commitment that cites those data-platform operational findings.

Owen's reconciliation changes purchasing from permitted spot capacity to a non-spot mode and changes the monthly cap from $18,000 to exactly $14,000, requiring a commitment that cites the FinOps reconciliation findings.

Leah's classification review changes the shared compute pool to a dedicated pool and changes audit retention from 30 to exactly 180 days, requiring a commitment that cites the security and compliance requirements.
